Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. MFA No.102569/2014 is filed by the insurance company and MFA.CROB No.100044/2022 is filed by the claimant.

Both the appeals are arising out of judgment and award dated 28.06.2014 passed in MVC No.179/2012 on the file of III Addl. Senior Civil and AMACT, Dharwad (for short,
'Tribunal').
3. Heard the learned counsel Sri.M.K. Soudagar, appearing for the appellant/insurance company and learned counsel Smt. Chetana S Biraj, appearing for the claimant/cross- objector.
4.

entities.text: III Addl. Senior Civil and AMACT, Dharwad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant/insurance company submits that the Tribunal has committed grave error in assessing the income, disability and award of compensation under the heads of medical expenses, towards the vehicle damage and laid-up period are on the higher side and seeks to reduce the same appropriately by taking note of the nature of disability suffered by the appellant and treatment provided to NC: 2024:KHC-D:6447 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100044 of 2022 him.

Hence, he seeks to allow the appeal filed by the insurance company.
5.

Per contra, learned counsel Smt. Chetana S Biraj, appearing for the claimant/cross-objector submits that the appellant sustained fractures of:
i. Compound communicated fracture shaft right femur lower end with intra articular extension.
ii. Inter condylar fracture upper end right tibia.
iii. Muscle tear.
Further, she submits that appellant underwent four surgeries.
Hence, the award of compensation by the Tribunal is just and appropriate and does not call for any modification.
She submits that the Tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the injured/appellant at Rs.4,500/- per month which she seeks to re-assess the same.

I have heard the argument of learned counsel for the appellant/insurance company and learned counsel for the claimant/cross-objector and perused the material available on record.

The cross-objector met with a road accident on 28.09.2011 and sustained fractures referred supra.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:6447 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100044 of 2022 7.

In support of his claim, he entered the witness box and deposed as PW1 and also examined Dr.Suresh Korlhalli as PW2 who has provided treatment to the claimant and produced 23 documents as Ex.P1 to P23.
Considering the oral evidence and documentary evidence on record, the Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- to the claimant.

This Court taking note of the injury suffered by the claimant and considering the oral testimony of the PW2 is of the considered view that the Tribunal has justified in assessing the disability of the claimant at 15%
which is unaltered.
This Court re-assess the notional income of the injured at Rs.6,000/- per month by placing reliance on the notional income chart prepared by KSLSA.
There is no dispute with regard to age of the appellant as 20 years, proper multiplier would be 18 and disability of the appellant at 15%.

Thus, loss of future income due to disability is recomputed as under:
6,000 x 12 x 18 x 15% =1,94,400/-
8.
Insofar as award of compensation under the head of loss of amenities, pain and sufferings are unaltered.

Under the head of medical expenses, it is modified by re-calculating bills produced by the claimants and the claimant would be entitled NC:
2 0 2 4 : K H C - D : 6 4 4 7 C / W M F A . C R O B N o . 1 0 0 0 4 4 o f 2 0 2 2 t o Rs.1,32,500/-(1,37,200-4,700).
Insofar as award of compensation under the head of loss of income during the laid- up period is unaltered, for the fact that the claimant was operated on four occasions.
There is no evidence with regard to the entitlement of compensation under the head of future medical expenses and operation.
Hence, the appellant would not be entitled to compensation for the aforesaid head.
Insofar as the award of compensation under the head of food and nourishment is unaltered.

This court keeping in mind, Ex.P5-the M.V. report and taking note of damage caused to the vehicle,
re-assess the entitlement of compensation towards the vehicle damage to Rs.20,000/-.

Thus, in all,
the claimant shall be entitled to modified compensation under the following heads:
 HEADS AMOUNT  (in Rs.)
Towards loss of future earnings 1,94,400/-

Towards loss of amenities 50,000/-
Towards pain and suffering 50,000/-
Towards medical expenses 1,32,500/-

Towards loss of income during laid-up 27,000/-
period Towards food and nourishment 25,000/-
Towards vehicle damage 20,000/-
 Total 4,98,900/-
